report.tagline: A UK food and grocery delivery app that brings meals from local restaurants and shops to your door in about 30 minutes, now owned by DoorDash.
report.simpleSummary: Deliveroo is an app for ordering takeaway. You pick a restaurant or a shop, order, and a rider on a bike or scooter brings it to you, usually in 20 to 40 minutes. Deliveroo takes a cut from the restaurant and charges you a delivery and service fee. It started in London in 2013 and was bought by the US company DoorDash in 2025.

overview.whatItDoes: Deliveroo connects hungry customers, restaurants and self-employed riders. Customers order in the app, restaurants cook, and riders deliver. It also delivers groceries from supermarkets and its own 'Hop' grocery stores, and runs 'Editions' kitchens for brands that want to cook in new areas.
howItWorks: You open the app and see restaurants and shops that can reach you, with delivery time and fee.
You order and pay in the app; Deliveroo sends the order to the restaurant's tablet.
A self-employed rider is matched to the order and picks it up when it is ready.
The rider delivers; you can track them live on a map.
Deliveroo Plus members pay a monthly fee for free delivery on orders above a minimum.
Restaurants pay Deliveroo a commission on each order, often around 25 to 35% if Deliveroo delivers.
overview.valueProposition: Meals from local favourite restaurants, and groceries, delivered fast, without needing to cook or go out.

businessModel.summary: Deliveroo takes a commission from restaurants and charges customers delivery and service fees. It pays riders per order. It earns more from ads, Plus memberships and groceries. Under DoorDash, it can share technology and cut costs.

revenueStreams.detail: A share of each order, often around 25 to 35% when Deliveroo delivers.
Delivery fees and a service fee on each order.
Restaurants and brands pay to appear higher or in promotions.
Margin on Hop and partner grocery orders.

businessModel.pricing: Delivery fees vary by distance and demand, often £0.99 to £3.99, plus a service fee. Deliveroo Plus costs about £3.49 to £7.99 a month depending on tier. Restaurant commissions are not public but often around 25 to 35%.
costDrivers: Running Hop grocery stores and Editions kitchens
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £25 order, the restaurant might pay Deliveroo about £7.50 in commission and the customer about £3 in delivery and service fees. That is about £10.50. The rider might be paid about £5, payments cost about £0.50, and refunds and support about £0.50. That leaves around £4 before marketing, tech and office costs. Deliveroo made its first tiny full-year profit in 2024, so margins per order are thin.

howTheyGetUsers: Deliveroo Plus partnerships, such as with Amazon Prime in the UK
whatBringsUsersBack: Favourite restaurants saved in the app
growth.moat: Deliveroo's moat is local: in each city, it has many restaurants, many riders and many customers. More customers attract more restaurants and riders, which makes delivery faster. DoorDash's tech and scale should help, but Uber Eats and Just Eat have similar networks in the UK.

competitors.name: Uber Eats
competitors.positioning: Global delivery app linked to Uber rides.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Deliveroo is stronger with premium restaurants in London; Uber Eats has a bigger global brand.

competitors.name: Just Eat
competitors.positioning: UK's oldest delivery app, now owned by Prosus.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Just Eat started as a marketplace where restaurants deliver themselves; Deliveroo built its own rider network.

competitors.name: Swiggy and Zomato (India)
competitors.positioning: Indian food delivery leaders with quick commerce.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Similar model but much lower order values; Indian apps rely more on ads and quick grocery delivery.

competitors.name: Supermarket delivery
competitors.positioning: Tesco Whoosh and others for groceries.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Deliveroo covers restaurants and groceries in one app.

northStar.metric: Weekly orders delivered on time and without complaint
northStar.why: Each good order means a happy customer, a paid restaurant and a paid rider. It shows that the marketplace is working for all three groups.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show the full cost, including all fees, before choosing a restaurant.
improvementIdeas.problem: Customers are annoyed by fees at checkout.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer abandoned orders and more trust.

improvementIdeas.idea: Photo proof of delivery and AI address checks.
improvementIdeas.problem: Riders cannot find addresses, leading to late or missing orders.

improvementIdeas.idea: Restaurant dashboard showing which dishes get complaints.
Pay riders for waiting time at restaurants.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More riders available and better pay.

pmLessons: Marketplaces with three sides (customers, restaurants, riders) must balance all three, or one side leaves.
Thin margins mean small changes in fees, pay or refunds can decide profit or loss.
Subscriptions like Plus can raise order frequency, but must pay for themselves.
Being bought by a bigger rival can bring scale, but also exits from smaller markets.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase order frequency on Deliveroo?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment customers. Ideas: Plus, grocery, personal offers. Measure orders per customer.

interviewQuestions.question: How should DoorDash integrate Deliveroo?
interviewQuestions.hint: Share tech, keep brand. Watch customer and rider impact. Set metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to reduce late deliveries.
interviewQuestions.hint: Find causes: rider supply, restaurant prep, address issues. Pick one and propose a fix.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Deliveroo with Swiggy and Zomato.
interviewQuestions.hint: Order values, fees, quick commerce, ads. Discuss what each could learn.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Deliveroo raise restaurant commission?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh revenue against restaurant churn. Model impact. Suggest tests.
